meta.title: Knowledge-to-care-to-payment flow
meta.principle: Clinical terminologies preserve meaning; classifications summarize it; billing codes report services; payer rules determine payment.
meta.summary: The semantic layer connects medical knowledge to the detailed clinical record before information is exchanged, classified for reporting, or adjudicated by a payer.
meta.disclaimer: Educational orientation only. These descriptions do not replace implementation guides, terminology licenses, coding rules, payer manuals, or clinical documentation requirements.

flow_stages.title: Medical science
flow_stages.question: What domain is being studied?
flow_stages.description: Disciplines and research domains organize expertise around systems, diseases, methods, populations, and biological scale.

flow_stages.title: Clinical record
flow_stages.question: What happened to this patient?
flow_stages.description: Narrative, findings, diagnoses, orders, results, procedures, medications, images, and context form the source record.

flow_stages.title: Clinical semantics
flow_stages.question: What does each clinical statement mean?
flow_stages.description: Reference terminologies and domain vocabularies preserve computable meaning before it is compressed into reporting or billing categories.

flow_stages.title: Interoperability
flow_stages.question: How does meaning move between systems?
flow_stages.description: Information models and exchange standards package coded clinical content into interoperable records and imaging objects.

flow_stages.title: Administrative coding
flow_stages.question: How is the encounter classified and billed?
flow_stages.description: Diagnosis, procedure, service, product, and claim-context codes support reporting and reimbursement workflows.

flow_stages.title: Maryland Medicaid
flow_stages.question: Is the claim covered and payable?
flow_stages.description: Program rules, provider manuals, authorization, managed-care contracts, fee schedules, and edits determine payment.

flow_stages.title: Adjudication & learning
flow_stages.question: What was paid, denied, measured, and learned?
flow_stages.description: Claims, outcomes, and real-world evidence flow back into operations, population health, research, and policy.

systems.name: Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine — Clinical Terms
systems.question: What clinical concept is being asserted?
systems.scope: Detailed, logic-based representation of disorders, findings, procedures, body structures, organisms, substances, situations, and other clinical content.
systems.note: The semantic center of the map: rich clinical meaning should not be reduced prematurely to a billing classification.

systems.name: Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes
systems.question: What was measured, observed, or documented?
systems.scope: Identifiers for laboratory tests, clinical observations, measurements, panels, surveys, and documents.
systems.note: LOINC generally identifies the observation; the result value and interpretation are carried separately.

systems.name: RxNorm normalized drug terminology
systems.question: Which clinical drug, ingredient, strength, and dose form is meant?
systems.scope: Normalized names and identifiers for generic and branded clinical drugs, with links to other drug vocabularies.
systems.note: RxNorm represents the medication concept; NDC identifies a particular labeled product and package.

systems.name: Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources
systems.question: How is coded clinical information packaged and exchanged?
systems.scope: Resources such as Condition, Observation, Procedure, MedicationRequest, DiagnosticReport, ImagingStudy, Claim, and ExplanationOfBenefit.
systems.note: FHIR is an exchange and information model, not a replacement for SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm, ICD, or other code systems.

systems.name: Unified Medical Language System
systems.question: How can concepts from different vocabularies be related?
systems.scope: Files and software that bring together many biomedical vocabularies, names, identifiers, and relationships to support interoperability.
systems.note: A crosswalk is not necessarily one-to-one; mappings can depend on context, purpose, release, and direction.

systems.name: Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine
systems.question: How are medical images and related information represented and exchanged?
systems.scope: Transmission, storage, retrieval, processing, and display of medical imaging information and associated metadata.
systems.steward: DICOM Standards Committee / Medical Imaging & Technology Alliance
systems.note: DICOM carries imaging objects and metadata; clinical concepts around them may still use SNOMED CT, LOINC, and FHIR bindings.

systems.name: GA4GH Variation Representation Specification
systems.question: How is a genomic variation represented precisely across systems?
systems.scope: A community specification for precise, interoperable representation and exchange of genetic variation data.
systems.steward: Global Alliance for Genomics and Health
systems.note: Genomic meaning also depends on reference sequences, gene nomenclature, evidence assertions, and clinical interpretation.

systems.name: Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model
systems.question: How can observational health data be standardized for analysis?
systems.scope: A common structure and standardized vocabularies for observational data used in outcomes research and real-world evidence.
systems.note: OMOP supports secondary analysis; it does not replace the source clinical record or transaction standards.
